title: After Tianjin Explosions, People Demand Answers

image.attribution: Voice of America/美国之音 / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
Public anger is growing in China following last week’s deadly explosions at a warehouse in the northern port city of Tianjin.

On Monday, angry residents gathered outside a building where Tianjin officials spoke to the media.

The residents are asking the government to hold talks with them and provide answers about what happened. The explosions have forced about 6,000 people to leave their homes.

Officials did not give clear answers about what the government plans to do to help displaced residents. They say they are investigating the disaster. And, they say, if they learn that anyone violated the law, they will punish whoever is responsible.

Many are asking why a warehouse that contained dangerous chemicals was permitted to operate so close to people’s houses. Chinese media have suggested the answer is political connections.

A study at the time found the site had some environmental risks, but it was safe enough to operate.

Now, people are growing concerned about the possible spread of sodium cyanide following the blast. The explosion also included a deadly combination of other dangerous chemicals.

questions.question: Where in China did the explosions happen?
What did the Chinese media say about the fact that the warehouse normally operated so close to the people’s houses?
options: It may have been a safety oversight.
It was a common practice in the area.
It was due to political connections.
It is an acceptable risk for industrial zones.
questions.answer: It was due to political connections.

questions.question: What are people growing concerned about?
options: The cleanup process of the site
The economic impact on the city
The possible spread of sodium cyanide
The anonymity of the warehouse owners
questions.answer: The possible spread of sodium cyanide
